title: Where 10,000 steps really comes from
summary: The 10,000-step goal traces back to a 1960s Japanese pedometer. Large studies suggest health benefits level off around 6,000–8,000 steps for older adults and 8,000–10,000 for younger adults.
evidenceNote: The step-count findings come from observational studies, which show associations rather than proof of cause. The marketing origin of '10,000' is widely reported by researchers.

scenes.text: Where does the 10,000-step goal come from?
scenes.answer: A 1960s Japanese pedometer called 'manpo-kei' — literally '10,000-step meter'.

scenes.text: The number was catchy. It wasn't based on a study.
In 2022, researchers pooled 15 studies covering 47,471 adults to test step counts against risk of death.
Risk fell as steps rose — then levelled off.
The biggest gains came for people moving from very few steps to a few more.
Forget the magic number. Aim for a little more than yesterday.

sources.title: Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts
sources.publisher: The Lancet Public Health (Paluch et al.)
